title: A test-author can work in its own -red checkout, or the red-run flow stops making one
why: Lane notes-fix-large-1 ([ended:lane:-notes-fix-large-1]), seen 3 times on Nov 9 (00:37, 03:33, 04:31 CST): test-authors make the `.claude/worktrees/agent-<id>-red` checkout that check_red_run.py expects, then the other-checkout guard refuses their cd and git calls into it, and its remedy sends them to their own worktree. They run the red run there and leave the -red checkout behind, unused. A guard that refuses a sanctioned act is a possible false alarm (rule verification-cry-wolf-guard-is-spent).
note: Coordinator pick a, 04:33 CST Nov 9 (process only): the other-checkout guard treats an agent's own -red checkout as its own, through guard.py _own_red_run, because check_red_run.py expects that checkout; the refusal is a false alarm, and route b would change the red-run flow the check relies on. A build lane, started after batch 68 merges. Related: step red-checkout-restore-absolute (a restore meant for -red landed in the agent's own worktree). Batch 68 merged (#2449, 11:55 CST Nov 9): free to start. Lane [ended:Lane-red-checkout-own-cd] started 12:13 CST Nov 9 (coordinator). Done (coordinator 12:31 CST Nov 9): _own_red_run (commit 5a202f078, batch 65g, 19:01 CST Nov 8) predates the three Nov 9 incidents, and the lane's probe on main allows all nine acts. Unmeasured: why the Nov 9 refusals happened; likely an install older than batch 65g. If the refusal comes back, reopen with the guard.log line.
